When Should You Replace Your AC?

settings.editor:
We won't sell you a system you don't need. However, at a certain point, repairing an old unit becomes more expensive than replacing it.

Our certified technicians help you evaluate your system’s health using these four critical factors:

icon_list.text: The Age Factor: Most air conditioners last 12 to 15 years. If yours is in that range, it’s statistically likely to face a major, expensive failure soon.
Refrigerant Costs: If your system uses outdated R-22 (Freon), simple recharges are becoming unsustainably expensive.
Frequency of Failure: If you’ve called for repairs more than once in the last two summers, your system is likely nearing total failure.
Energy Efficiency: Modern SEER2 systems can slash your utility bills by up to 40% compared to units from just a decade ago.

settings.editor: The "Rule of $5,000" is a simple formula: multiply the age of your AC by the repair cost; if the total exceeds $5,000, you should replace the unit. For example, if a 10-year-old system needs a $600 repair ($6,000 total), the math suggests that investing in a new, high-efficiency unit is a smarter financial move than patching an aging system.

Most standard AC replacements are completed in a single day, typically taking between 6 and 10 hours. Our team arrives early to prep the site and does not leave until your new system is fully calibrated, the air is cool, and the workspace is spotless.

Yes, upgrading to a modern SEER2-rated unit can lower your summer cooling costs by 20% to 40%. Older systems work significantly harder to move heat, consuming more electricity. Modern high-efficiency units use advanced compressor technology to provide better cooling while using a fraction of the power.
